ibr-version-literals.mechanism: The CLI hard-codes .version("0.8.0") and the MCP server hard-codes SERVER_INFO.version "0.4.9" while package.json says 1.0.0, so `ibr --version` and MCP clients report wrong, mutually inconsistent versions instead of reading the manifest.

bl-maintainer-path-default.mechanism: DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_BUILD falls back to the maintainer's /Users/... checkout path when IBR_DASHBOARD_BUILD is unset, so on any other machine the build step cannot find the script and fails.

nav-receiver-regex.cls: hand-written regex duplicates the call-pattern table
nav-receiver-regex.mechanism: The receiver regex is maintained separately from SDK_DEFINITIONS call patterns; its optional dotted group captures "openai.chat" for openai.chat.completions.create, so the client-variable lookup misses and the most common OpenAI call shape emits no LLM-call anchor.

arp-factkind-spelling.cls: hand-written spelling table drifted from serde wire names
arp-factkind-spelling.mechanism: serde rename_all=snake_case writes BacklogItem as "backlog_item" but FactKind::parse accepts only "backlog-item", so passing a kind read from the ledger to `rally say` fails as an unsupported fact kind.

bl-codex-manifest-version.cls: duplicated version left behind on release
bl-codex-manifest-version.mechanism: The release bump moved .claude-plugin/plugin.json and package.json to 0.42.1 but .codex-plugin/plugin.json stayed at 0.42.0 although bump_version.py lists it as an owned surface, so Codex installs advertise a stale version.

bl-rally-kind-allowlist.cls: other component's vocabulary copied as a literal
bl-rally-kind-allowlist.mechanism: _native_kind trusts a hard-coded set of kinds the rally binary supposedly accepts, and the capability probe only checks that `say` exists, so a binary build lacking a kind rejects it after the local ledger append succeeded and the Rally projection is silently lost.

bl-learn-wrong-duplicate-row.cls: two readers resolve duplicate rows differently
bl-learn-wrong-duplicate-row.mechanism: When a run_id owns two runs[] rows, Learn stamps the FIRST matching row while run_close_lint grades the LAST, so --require-learn reports learn_missing for a run that finished Learn.

arp-daemon-hop-drops-fields.mechanism: When rallyd is running, the snapshot crosses the daemon wire via the public serializer, so its #[serde(skip)] internal fields arrive defaulted; checkpoints get seq 0, repeated `next` appends duplicate wake intents and stale-author demotion stops, unlike the direct path.
